label: early copy phase, b/f/0 being output now or next
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, right after the delimiter: about 63% of mass at recall_idx 1 (input is the echoed first token) and 32% at recall_idx 2, with almost nothing past recall_idx 3 and never in the original or delimiter phases. Inside that window it is strongly tied to the tokens being output now or next: b (current-output lift 9.8x, next-output lift 11.9x), then f and 0, with weaker preference for d/s/i/z/a/j. Magnitude is graded: the strongest activations (about 0.8-1.0 of max) come when both the current and next outputs are in {b,f,0}. That conjunction has 0.82 precision but covers only about 17% of mass. When neither is in the set, activations stay weak. Shorter sequences (L 4-6) fire more often. It does not depend on the input token identity, digit count or first token. Precision of the predicate is low: many early-copy steps with b/f/0 upcoming stay inactive, so the token set is only a partial description of the selectivity.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: b, 0, f, s, d, a; least: 2, o, x, t) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: b, f, 0, s; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, recall_idx=2, recall_idx=3.
